 Los Angeles’ most expensive private schools give wealthy students privileges most public school kids can only dream of
 Los Angeles’ most expensive private schools charge nearly ninety thousand dollars in annual tuition, surpassing even the cost of public universities. 
 These elite schools provide astonishing privileges like on-campus paleontology museums, real investment portfolios and Hollywood mentors within their elite education. 
 Celebrities like LeBron James and Arnold Schwarzenegger choose these exclusive institutions to educate their children in California. 
 Elite schools with tuition fees exceeding the cost of a college degree 
 While millions of families struggle to afford higher education, Los Angeles’ most expensive private schools charge annual tuition fees approaching ninety thousand dollars to attend high school, far exceeding the budget required to study at prestigious institutions like UCLA . Thus, topping this exclusive list in Southern California sits The Webb Schools in Claremont, where boarding students pay over eighty-seven thousand dollars per year to access a one-hundred-fifty-acre campus featuring an Olympic-size pool and the only accredited paleontology museum on a high school campus, among other privileges. Likewise, an analysis of the twenty costliest institutions in the region demonstrates that sixteen of them demand base payments exceeding fifty-three thousand dollars annually, adding extra fees for private security, cutting-edge technology, and school transportation all for elite education.

 Scientific expeditions, real finance and direct Hollywood mentors 
 Similarly, the sky-high tuition prices at Los Angeles’ most expensive private schools translate into academic privileges and hands-on experiences that the vast majority of public school students can barely imagine. For example, within this elite education at centers like Milken Community School , whose tuition exceeds fifty-seven thousand dollars annually, teenagers manage real investment portfolios under expert financial mentorship and take screenwriting and comedy classes that renowned Hollywood director Jon Avnet teaches. On the other hand, institutions like Westmark School in Encino, California charge nearly seventy thousand dollars to offer ultra-small classrooms of eight students on a net-zero-carbon campus with rooftop gardens, while at Webb young people collaborate with professional paleontologists and co-author scientific papers.

 The celebrity magnet and social exclusivity in Southern California 
 Beyond academic prestige and top-tier facilities for elite education, Los Angeles’ most expensive private schools function as genuine social clubs where the children of major Hollywood stars and real estate moguls share desks. In this way, iconic institutions like Crossroads School in Santa Monica or The Buckley School educated figures like Kim Kardashian , Gwyneth Paltrow , and LeBron James ‘ children, consolidating a privileged network of contacts since adolescence. Although several of these schools allocate millions of dollars in financial aid to attract diverse talent, for families paying full tuition rates, this elite education represents a multi-million-dollar investment that marks an abysmal gap against the public system across The United States.
 The 10 most expensive private schools in Los Angeles 
 The Webb Schools (Claremont) : Charges eighty-seven thousand four hundred thirty dollars for boarding students and sixty-two thousand one hundred eighty dollars for day students, housing the only accredited paleontology museum on a high school campus.
 Westmark School (Encino) : Charges sixty-nine thousand nine hundred twenty-eight dollars annually, featuring a lower-school campus with rooftop gardens and net-zero-carbon design.
 New Roads School (Santa Monica) : Charges sixty-nine thousand four hundred dollars for its specialized Spectrum Program and fifty-five thousand fourteen dollars for grades six through twelve.
 The Buckley School (Sherman Oaks) : Charges fifty-eight thousand seven hundred eighty-eight dollars annually, counting figures like Paris Hilton and Kim Kardashian among its alumni.
 Crossroads School (Santa Monica) : Charges fifty-eight thousand five hundred forty-one dollars per year, having educated Hollywood stars like Kate Hudson, Jonah Hill, and Gwyneth Paltrow.
 Brentwood School : Charges fifty-eight thousand two hundred seven dollars annually, welcoming the children of Arnold Schwarzenegger and developer Rick Caruso among its former students.
 Oakwood School (North Hollywood) : Charges fifty-seven thousand five hundred fifty dollars per year for its exclusive academic program.
 Milken Community School : Charges fifty-seven thousand four hundred fifty dollars annually plus a two-thousand-seven-hundred-dollar security fee, allowing students to manage a real investment portfolio.
 Campbell Hall (Studio City) : Charges fifty-seven thousand eighty dollars per year, counting NBA star Jrue Holiday as one of its notable graduates.
 Harvard-Westlake : Charges fifty-four thousand nine hundred dollars annually, boasting astronaut Sally Ride and actress Carrie Fisher among its distinguished alumni.
